purpose: Return canonical LIVE state mutation events or recent activity from the LIVE event journal.
parameters: after_revision (integer or null, optional, default null): filter canonical LIVE state mutation events strictly newer than this canonical revision integer; omit for initial/latest polling of recent journal events.
limit (integer or null, optional, default 20): maximum retained events to return; pass null for all retained events.
behavior:
MCP cannot push unsolicited messages into an idle model; this bounded
feed is the reliable pull mechanism for continuous LIVE state.
Events are an ephemeral in-RAM notification feed retained in a shared journal
(retaining the most recent 10,000 mixed activity records), not a persistent full history
or append-only source of truth. The canonical LIVE state is authoritative.
The response exposes explicit continuity metadata: ``latest_revision`` (authoritative canonical revision),
``earliest_retained_revision`` (or ``null`` if buffer empty), ``continuity``
(``'not_requested'``, ``'continuous'``, or ``'gap'``), ``resync_required`` (boolean),
and ``resync_reason`` (``'event_retention_gap'``, ``'revision_discontinuity'``, or ``null``).
When ``after_revision`` is supplied, only canonical mutation events (publish and update_file) are returned;
MCP tool calls and non-canonical activity events are excluded. When ``after_revision`` is omitted (null),
the most recent retained mixed activity events from the journal are returned with ``continuity='not_requested'``.
The sequence cursor (``after_seq``) is used internally by Desktop activity feeds and is not part of this public tool schema.
When ``resync_required=true``, the caller cursor lost continuity with the retained event window;
the caller must perform a canonical state resync (e.g. query_canonical_projection or
get_project_architecture) rather than assuming returned events represent a complete sequential delta.
``limit=None`` returns all retained matching events within the journal window, not the full history.
``truncated`` indicates truncation solely due to the requested ``limit``, not retention loss.
errors:
Events are retained in RAM by the shared LIVE owner (most recent 10,000 records).
Each canonical full-analysis event identifies its ``origin`` (``desktop_analysis``,
``mcp_analysis`` or ``cli_analysis``); incremental watcher events use
``desktop_watcher``. Events also identify operation, status and file path. Update
events additionally expose ``blast_radius_state`` and a bounded
``affected_modules`` collection (hard limit of 20 items in journal).
Syntax failures additionally expose ``error``, ``line_number`` and
``column_number``.
usage_notes:
LLM workflow after every file edit:
- If the desktop app is running, do *not* call ``update_file``. Its watcher
  owns the update. Poll this tool with the last observed revision until the
  desktop event arrives, then react to its status before further edits.
- If the desktop app is not running, call ``update_file`` after every edit,
  then call this tool to confirm the revision and diagnostics.
- If ``resync_required=true`` is returned, do not assume unbroken event history;
  perform a canonical state sync using query_canonical_projection.
